1: # What Cloudflare logs about a Worker request by default
2: 
3: Research for issue #10 (map #1). Throwaway branch, not for merging. Researched 2026-11-07 against developers.cloudflare.com and cloudflare.com.
4: 
5: **Why it matters.** SPEC §5.3 says request logs for the Submission endpoint must not contain the Invitation token, the Person, or the IP address together with the Submission. SPEC §6.4 sends errors and traces to Workers Logs and Workers Observability. SPEC §7 makes "logs from the submission path contain no identifiers" a release-blocking test. (The ticket also names GLOSSARY.md, but that file does not exist on `origin/main` yet.)
6: 
7: ## TL;DR
8: 
9: 1. **The default is on.** New Workers have `observability.enabled = true`, and `head_sampling_rate` defaults to 1. Every request gets an *invocation log*, labelled `Fetch <METHOD> <URL>`, with the full URL including the query string. The log also holds request and response metadata that Cloudflare does not fully document. Paid plans keep these logs for 7 days, the Free plan for 3.
10: 2. **Traces are opt-in** (`observability.traces.enabled`). Once on, the inbound span records `url.full`, the full user agent, `cloudflare.ray_id`, ASN, and geo down to city. D1 and Durable Object SQL spans record `db.query.text`. The docs list no client IP attribute on spans.
11: 3. **Tail Workers, `wrangler tail` and Logpush trace events carry `event.request.url` and `headers`.** Cloudflare's docs describe redaction only for the `tail()` handler. There it covers a fixed list of header names and ID-shaped substrings of the URL. `cf-connecting-ip` and `x-forwarded-for` are **not** on that list, and `getUnredacted()` bypasses all of it.
12: 4. **The edge always writes an HTTP request log line**, with `ClientIP`, `ClientRequestURI` (path plus query) and `RayID`. A customer cannot stop the edge from writing it. A customer can only choose not to retain it (Logpull, off by default, 3 to 7 days) or not to push it (Logpush). Cloudflare publishes no fixed retention period for its own internal copy.
13: 5. **Analytics Engine records only what `writeDataPoint` writes**, and keeps it 3 months. AI Gateway logs prompts and responses **by default**. Turnstile processes the client IP, TLS fingerprint and user agent.
14: 6. **Design consequence.** Never put the Invitation token in the Submission URL. Send it in the POST body, or better, exchange it in an earlier request for a short-lived, unlinkable submission credential. Serve the Submission endpoint from its own Worker with `invocation_logs = false`, traces off, no `tail_consumers` and `logpush = false`. Sampling is per Worker or per environment, not per route. Test the result empirically, because Cloudflare does not publish the full field list of an invocation log.
15: 
16: ## 1. Workers Logs (persisted logs)
17: 
18: Source: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/workers-logs/>
19: 
20: - **Default on.** "Newly created Workers have it on by default." The `observability.enabled` key is shorthand for `logs.enabled`, "defaults to `true` for all new Workers", and makes the logs persist ([Wrangler configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/)).
21: - **Invocation log.** "Each Workers invocation returns a single invocation log that contains details such as the Request, Response, and related metadata". These logs are identified by `$cloudflare.$metadata.type = "cf-worker-event"`. Each one is "enriched with information available to Cloudflare in the context of the invocation". A fetch invocation is shown as `Fetch <Method> <URL>`, so **the URL, query string included, is in the log**.
22: - **Request ID and Ray ID.** The Observability API schema defines `rayId` as the "Cloudflare Ray ID from the cf-ray header of the request that triggered the invocation", and `requestId` as the ID "that ties all logs from a single invocation together" ([API reference](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/workers/subresources/observability/)). Each event also carries timestamps and duration (`$metadata.endTime` and `duration`), plus the account and service.
23: - **Not documented.** Cloudflare does not publish the complete field list of an invocation log. In particular, it does not say whether request headers or the `cf` object are stored, or whether redaction applies. Treat both as **unknown until verified** (see section 9).
24: - **Custom logs.** Every `console.log` line is stored and linked to the invocation by `requestId` and `rayId`. So any value logged on the Submission path ends up in the same log group as the URL and the Ray ID.
25: - **Turning it off or down:**
26:   ```toml
27:   [observability]
28:   enabled = true          # false = do not persist logs for this Worker
29:   head_sampling_rate = 1  # 0..1, per Worker, default 1
30: 
31:   [observability.logs]
32:   invocation_logs = false # keep console.log output, drop the automatic invocation log
33:   ```
34:   Per-environment overrides go under `[env.<name>.observability]`, and `observability` is an inheritable key. **There is no per-route setting.** Sampling is head-based per request: "When a request is sampled, all logs for that request are kept." Above the daily limit, Cloudflare applies a 1% head sample for the rest of the day.
35: - **Retention.** 3 days on Free, 7 days on Paid ("the stated maximum"). The maximum log size is 256 KB, and larger logs are truncated with `$cloudflare.truncated = true`.
36: 
37: ## 2. Workers Observability: traces
38: 
39: Sources: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/spans-and-attributes/>
40: 
41: - **Opt-in.** Turn traces on with `[observability.traces] enabled = true`. The docs say that `observability.enabled = true` "currently enables logs only, not traces". `head_sampling_rate` takes 0 to 1 and defaults to 1 once traces are on. Logs and traces can use different sampling rates. Traces are kept for 7 days.
42: - **Inbound fetch handler span:** `http.request.method`, `url.full`, `url.path`, `network.protocol.name`, `http.request.header.accept`, `accept-encoding`, `accept-language`, `user_agent.original` plus parsed browser, OS and device fields, `cloudflare.asn`, `cloudflare.verified_bot_category`, `geo.timezone`, `geo.continent.code`, `geo.country.code`, `geo.locality.name`, `geo.locality.region`. The root span also gets `cloudflare.ray_id`, and all spans get `cloudflare.colo`.
43: - **No IP attribute is listed** on any span.
44: - **Outbound fetch spans** record `url.full`, `url.query`, `server.address`, a few content headers, and the body sizes.
45: - **Binding spans.** D1 and Durable Object SQL spans record **`db.query.text`**. If the SQL is parameterized, the text holds `?` placeholders, but string-interpolated values would end up in the trace. KV spans record the keys (`cloudflare.kv.query.keys`). A token used as a KV or D1 lookup key would therefore show up in the trace of the lookup request. Durable Object spans record `cloudflare.durable_object.id`.
46: - **Privacy reading.** Even without an IP, the combination of `url.full`, the full user agent, ASN, city, Ray ID and timestamp is close to identifying for a small team. In the Submission Worker, turn traces off.
47: 
48: ## 3. Real-time logs (`wrangler tail`, dashboard Live view)
49: 
50: Source: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/real-time-logs/>
51: 
52: - Real-time logs exist only while someone is tailing: "Real-time logs does not store Workers Logs." Each event is JSON with `outcome`, `scriptName`, `exceptions`, `logs`, `eventTimestamp`, and `event.request.{url, method, headers, cf}`.
53: - Anyone with access to the account can tail any Worker at any time, so this is an access-control concern rather than a retention one. The page does not say whether `wrangler tail` applies the redaction from section 4.
54: 
55: ## 4. Tail Workers
56: 
57: Sources: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/tail-workers/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/handlers/tail/>
58: 
59: - **Opt-in** per producer, through `tail_consumers`. That key is not inheritable, so each environment declares its own.
60: - A Tail Worker receives the same shape of event: request `url`, `method`, `headers` and `cf` (`IncomingRequestCfProperties`), plus logs, exceptions and diagnostics-channel events.
61: - **Default redaction**, as documented for the `tail()` handler's `TailRequest`:
62:   - **Headers.** A header's value becomes `"REDACTED"` when its name is `cookie` or `set-cookie`, or contains `auth`, `key`, `secret`, `token` or `jwt`, matched case-insensitively. **`cf-connecting-ip`, `x-forwarded-for` and `x-real-ip` do not match**, so the client IP passes through in the headers.
63:   - **URL.** Each greedily matched run of `[A-Za-z0-9+\-_]` is replaced when it is a hex ID (32 or more hex digits) or a base-64 ID (21 or more characters with at least 2 uppercase letters, 2 lowercase letters and 2 digits). A token shorter than that, or one without the right mix of characters (for example lowercase base32), is **not** redacted.
64:   - `getUnredacted()` returns the raw values. Redaction is a convenience, not a guarantee.
65: 
66: ## 5. Logpush
67: 
68: Sources: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/account/workers_trace_events/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/zone/http_requests/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/faq/worker-subrequests/>
69: 
70: - **Workers Trace Events** (account dataset). Pushing this dataset needs Workers Paid, a Logpush job, and **`logpush = true` in the Worker's config, which defaults to `false`**. The fields are `Event`, `EventTimestampMs`, `EventType`, `Logs`, `Exceptions`, `Outcome`, `ScriptName`, `ScriptTags`, `ScriptVersion`, `Entrypoint`, `DispatchNamespace`, `CPUTimeMs` and `WallTimeMs`. The docs do not specify what is inside `Event`. Assume it holds the same request shape as a tail event (URL, method, response status, possibly headers) until verified.
71: - **HTTP requests** (zone dataset). The Logpush overview says Logpush is now available on all plans, but which datasets you get depends on your products. The fields include **`ClientIP`**, **`ClientRequestURI`** ("includes the full path and query string"), `ClientRequestPath` (without the query string), `ClientRequestHost`, `ClientRequestUserAgent`, `ClientRequestReferer`, `RayID`, `ParentRayID`, `EdgeStartTimestamp`, `WorkerScriptName` and `WorkerSubrequest`. `RequestHeaders` and `Cookies` are populated only when custom fields are configured.
72: - **Both datasets are opt-in exports.** But the HTTP request record behind them exists either way (section 7). If you configure an HTTP requests job, either leave out `ClientIP` and `ClientRequestURI`, or filter out the Submission host.
73: 
74: ## 6. AI Gateway and Analytics Engine
75: 
76: - **AI Gateway** (<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/observability/logging/>). "Logs are enabled by default for each gateway". A log holds "the prompt, response, provider, timestamp, status, token usage, cost, duration, and user agent". You can turn logging off per gateway in Settings, or per request with `cf-aig-collect-log: false`. The header `cf-aig-collect-log-payload: false` keeps the metadata but drops the prompt and response bodies. Gateways created on or after 2026-09-24 follow the Workers Logs retention rules. This matters for comment redaction (§5.3, §6.1): **turn payload logging off on the gateway used for raw comments**, through Alchemy if it supports that, and send the header on every call as a second layer of protection.
77: - **Workers Analytics Engine** (<https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine/>, [limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine/limits/), [sampling](https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine/sampling/)). It is a write API: nothing is captured automatically. The docs describe no implicit IP or URL capture. Data is kept for **3 months**, and is sampled at write time and query time (`_sample_interval`). The only risk is what we write ourselves: never write a Person ID, a token or a Submission ID, and keep its index coarser than one team below N.
78: 
79: ## 7. What Cloudflare keeps that a customer cannot turn off
80: 
81: - **The edge HTTP request log.** Every proxied request produces a log line in Cloudflare's log pipeline, with default fields including "client IP, request host and method, URI, edge timestamps, response bytes and status, and a Ray ID" ([Logpull basics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpull/understanding-the-basics/)). A customer controls two things:
82:   - **Logpull retention**: "By default, your HTTP request logs are not retained." When it is turned on, logs can be queried "at least 3 days and up to 7 days" back. You turn it off with `POST /logs/control/retention/flag {"flag": false}`, and existing logs remain until they expire ([enabling log retention](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpull/enabling-log-retention/)).
83:   - **Logpush** exports.
84: - **Cloudflare's own processing.** The [privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/) says that for End Users, Cloudflare "processes data on behalf of its Customers", including "IP addresses, traffic routing data". Personal data is stored "for a period of time that is consistent with the business purposes", with **no fixed number** for edge logs. Separately, "Network Data" is used to identify and block malicious activity. The often-quoted "25 hours" applies only to the 1.1.1.1 resolver, not to Workers or zones. The [GDPR FAQ](https://www.cloudflare.com/trust-hub/gdpr/) says log metadata contains limited personal data, "most often in the form of IP addresses".
85: - **What follows for us.** We cannot prevent Cloudflare from seeing IP plus URL plus time for the Submission request. That is inherent to using a reverse proxy, and Cloudflare is our processor under the DPA. What we control is (a) **what the URL contains**, (b) **which logs we persist or export**, and (c) **whether the Submission request carries anything that links it to a Person**. The privacy page should say plainly that Cloudflare processes IP addresses as our processor for transport and security.
86: 
87: ## 8. Turnstile
88: 
89: Sources: [Turnstile Privacy Addendum](https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/), <https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/>, [server-side validation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/get-started/server-side-validation/)
90: 
91: - **Signals processed**: "client IP address, TLS Fingerprint, User-Agent Header and Sitekey and associated origin."
92: - **Cloudflare's role.** It is a **processor** when it protects our site, and a **controller** when it uses the signals to improve bot detection, under legitimate interest.
93: - **Retention.** The addendum gives no retention period.
94: - **What it does not read.** "Turnstile does not access, store, or transmit user communications, form entries, or other page inputs."
95: - **`siteverify`.** The parameters are `secret`, `response`, an optional `remoteip` and an optional `idempotency_key`. The response holds `hostname`, `challenge_ts`, `action`, `cdata` and `metadata.ephemeral_id` (Enterprise only), and contains no IP. Tokens are single-use and valid for 300 seconds.
96: - **For us:**
97:   - **Do not send `remoteip`.**
98:   - **Do not put anything that identifies a Person or Invitation in `cdata` or `action`.**
99:   - Turnstile protects only the public-link answer page (§6.2). It is not needed on the invitation path.
100: 
101: ## 9. Recommendations for SurveyBeat
102: 
103: 1. **Token out of the URL.** Email links can carry the token to the answer page, but that page load is a separate request from the Submission request. Better still, the answer page swaps the token (via `POST` body) for a short-lived, single-use submission credential that is not linked to the Person in any stored form. The Submission request then carries only that credential and the answers, in the body. The URL of the Submission request becomes a constant such as `POST /s`. This is the "separate requests" option in §5.3.
104: 2. **A separate Submission Worker is the cleaner boundary.** All of these settings work per Worker or per environment, never per route: `observability.enabled`, `logs.invocation_logs`, `head_sampling_rate`, `traces.enabled`, `tail_consumers` and `logpush`. A dedicated Worker on its own route or host lets us set, in Alchemy:
105:    - `observability.logs.invocation_logs = false`
106:    - traces off
107:    - no `tail_consumers`
108:    - `logpush = false`
109:    - custom logging limited to an allowlisted structured logger, with no request object, no headers and no IP.
110: 
111:    This fits §6.1's rule to "add more Workers only when a job needs a different runtime profile". The main Worker can keep full observability. If we keep one Worker, the only lever is to turn invocation logs off for **everything**.
112: 3. **IP never paired with a Submission in our own code.** Never read `cf-connecting-ip` on the Submission path. Do not pass it to Turnstile's `remoteip`. Do not write it to Analytics Engine.
113: 4. **SQL and KV hygiene.** Use parameterized statements only, so that `db.query.text` holds placeholders. Never use a token as a KV key on a traced path. Hash it, or keep traces off.
114: 5. **Edge log exports.** If Logpush for HTTP requests is ever configured, leave out `ClientIP` and `ClientRequestURI` for the Submission host, or filter that host out. Keep Logpull retention off, which is the default, and assert this in infrastructure code.
115: 6. **AI Gateway.** Turn payload logging off on the redaction gateway, and send `cf-aig-collect-log-payload: false` with each call.
116: 7. **Privacy test (§7), two layers:**
117:    - **Unit layer.** Make the Submission handler's logger an Effect service. Feed in a request carrying a token, a Person-like value and an IP. Assert that nothing captured contains them.
118:    - **Preview-stage layer.** Deploy, send one Submission, then query the Observability API (`/workers/observability/telemetry/query`) for that `rayId` or `scriptName`. Assert that there are no invocation logs and that no stored event contains the token, the IP or the Person ID.
119: 
120:    The preview-stage check also covers the gap in section 1: Cloudflare does not document whether invocation logs store headers. **This test is the authority, not this document.**
121: 
122: ## Open points and caveats
123: 
124: - Invocation logs: the full field list (headers? `cf`? redaction?) is undocumented. Settle it with the probe in recommendation 7 before implementation.
125: - Whether `wrangler tail` and Workers Logs apply the `TailRequest` redaction is undocumented.
126: - The Logpush overview says Logpush is available on all plans. Older docs limited zone HTTP requests to Enterprise. Check this for our plan if it matters.
127: - Cloudflare publishes no internal retention period for edge logs, and the Turnstile addendum gives none for its signals. If a fixed number is needed for the privacy page, it has to come from Cloudflare's DPA or support, not from the public docs.

1: # Preview stages are gated by what the revision changes
2: 
3: The preview workflow was the largest single CI cost, and it decided most of its work only after it had started. Every push deployed a stage, smoke tested it, read back its privacy settings and ran the end-to-end suite. That happened even when the pull request had already moved on, and even when the diff could not change a deployed byte.
4: 
5: ## Context
6: 
7: Baseline from `node scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs --days 7`, over the seven days to 2026-11-17:
8: 
9: | Workflow | Runs | Runner minutes | Per job |
10: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
11: | CI | 153 | 312 | check 1.6m, privacy 0.4m |
12: | Preview | 118 | 363 | deploy 1.2m, e2e 1.9m, preview-privacy 1.7m, destroy 0.7m |
13: | Deploy | 60 | 243 | staging deploy 0.8m, staging-e2e 1.0m, staging-privacy 1.9m, production 0.9m |
14: | All | | 918 (131 per day, about $31 per 30 days at $0.008 a minute) | |
15: 
16: A pull request's required answer arrives in about 90 seconds. The preview stage adds about 4.8 runner minutes and about five minutes of wall time per revision. The runners are GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`, so the money at stake is small. Feedback time and work nobody needs are the point.
17: 
18: The whole test suite is 82 test files and finishes in 18 seconds locally. At this size, sharding and dependency-based test selection would cost more than they save. What transfers is the order: decide before paying for setup, and make the decision inspectable and tested.
19: 
20: Backtest against this repository's last 100 preview runs:
21: 
22: - The superseded-revision guard would have skipped 2 of them (1.3 runner minutes). It pays when three or more pushes land inside one run's ~4.5 minutes, which is an agent loop rather than today's cadence.
23: - The prose-only gate covers 2 of them (8.9 runner minutes, about 4% of preview compute) and 7 of the last 100 pull requests. Documentation work is a real share of this repository's changes.
24: 
25: ## Decision
26: 
27: The preview workflow starts with a `select` job. It runs before checkout and before any install, and it sets four outputs: `head`, `stage`, `canary` and `lighthouse`.
28: 
29: - **Superseded guard.** The first step reads the pull request's current head SHA. If the revision is no longer the head, `head` is false and every later job in the run is skipped. A newer revision owns the stage. If the read fails, `head` is true: being unsure is a reason to run.
30: - **Path rules in tested code.** `scripts/ci/select.mjs` classifies the changed files, and `scripts/ci/select.test.ts` locks every rule. The canary rule (the Submission path) and the Lighthouse rule (the answer entry) are the regular expressions the workflow already used, moved verbatim. The canary also covers `scripts/ci/`, because a pull request that changes the gates must run them.
31: - **Changed files.** The list comes from the compare endpoint, addressed by the base and head SHAs of the pull request. It matches the old `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename, so a rename away from a gated path stays gated. The endpoint returns at most 300 changed files, and only on the first page. Pagination walks commits, not files. A response of 300 files keeps every gate, because that response is also what a longer diff looks like.
32: - **Prose-only gate.** `stage` is false only when the list is non-empty and every file is prose or tooling that cannot reach a deployed stage: under `docs/`, any `*.md` file, the agent instruction directories, `.githooks/`, `skills-lock.json`, or the root `scripts/` (not `infra/scripts/` and not `scripts/ci/`). An empty list, a mixed list or any other path deploys. A canary or Lighthouse path always keeps the stage, even when it is markdown.
33: - **Jobs.** `deploy` runs when `head` and `stage` are on. `preview-privacy` and `e2e` need `deploy`, so they skip with it. The canary sweep runs only when `canary` is on. The Lighthouse gate and its app build run only when `lighthouse` is on.
34: - **Failure modes.** A failed read of the pull request keeps the stage. A failed read of the changed files turns on all three gates.
35: 
36: `ci.yml` and `deploy.yml` do not change. Every pull request still runs the check job and the privacy job, and every merge to `main` still deploys staging and production.
37: 
38: ## Considered options
39: 
40: - **Gating the Deploy workflow by changed paths.** Rejected. A `workflow_run` payload does not say how many commits a push carried, so the tip's diff can miss a Submission-path change earlier in the same push. A privacy invariant is a release blocker (SPEC §7). Revisit only with a reliable push range, for example by diffing against the last deployed SHA.
41: - **`cancel-in-progress: true` on the preview group.** Rejected. It interrupts a half-applied Alchemy deploy or destroy. The revision guard removes the same waste without interrupting anything.
42: - **Workflow-level `paths:` filters.** Rejected. A filtered run reports no check at all, so a reviewer cannot tell "not needed" from "not reported".
43: - **Caching Playwright browsers in the `e2e` job.** Rejected for now. It is worth about 30 seconds per run. Measure it before adding a cache key.
44: - **Splitting the `check` job.** Rejected. The suite is the dominant step (62 seconds on a runner) and runs in parallel with nothing today. Splitting would buy about 25 seconds of wall time and pay for a second setup.
45: 
46: ## Consequences
47: 
48: - The path rules are code. A change to a rule fails `scripts/ci/select.test.ts` until the test is updated on purpose.
49: - The rules come from the revision under test, the same as the workflow file itself. A pull request that edits `scripts/ci/select.mjs` is classified by its own copy.
50: - A change to `scripts/ci/` always deploys and runs the canary sweep, because it changes the gates. Other root `scripts/` paths stay prose and do not deploy.
51: - The gate classifies the whole PR diff against its base, not the one push. So a stage deployed by an earlier revision stays until the PR closes, even if the diff later becomes prose-only. A prose-only revision does not tear it down.
52: - The effect on feedback time and compute is to be measured after a week of the new workflow, as the issue's step 6 says.

Based on the Steampipe Cloudflare plugin documentation, here are the descriptions and column details for the requested tables:

### 1. `cloudflare_worker_script`
Provides insights into metadata for Workers deployed per account within Cloudflare[1].
* **Notable Columns:**
  * `id` — The ID of the script in the Workers system (usually the script name)[2].
  * `account_id` — ID of the account the worker script belongs to.
  * `created_on` — Timestamp when the script was created.
  * `modified_on` — When the script was last modified[2].
  * `usage_model` — Usage model for the Worker invocations[2].
  * `has_assets` — Boolean flag indicating whether the worker has assets.
  * `has_modules` — Boolean flag indicating whether the worker uses modules.
  * `logpush` — Whether Logpush is turned on for the Worker[2].
  * `handlers` — Event handlers associated with the worker.
  * `placement` — Configuration for Smart Placement[2].
  * `subdomain` — JSON representing workers.dev subdomain mappings (or whether it is available on the `workers.dev` subdomain)[1][2].
  * `tail_consumers` — List of Workers that will consume logs from the attached Worker[2].
  * Standard Steampipe meta columns (`title`, `conn`, `_ctx`).

---

### 2. `cloudflare_zone_setting`
Represents individual zone settings that control various Cloudflare features for a specific zone[3].
* **Notable Columns:**
  * `zone_id` — ID of the zone the setting belongs to.
  * `zone_name` — Name of the zone.
  * `id` — ID or name of the setting (e.g., SSL, security level, cache level).
  * `value` — Value of the zone setting.
  * `editable` — Boolean indicating if the setting can be modified.
  * `modified_on` — Timestamp when the setting was last modified.
  * Standard Steampipe meta columns (`title`, `conn`, `_ctx`).

---

### 3. `cloudflare_logpush_job`
Configuration that automatically ships log data from a specific zone or account to a chosen external destination in near real-time batch delivery[3].
* **Notable Columns:**
  * `id` — Unique identifier of the Logpush job.
  * `account_id` — ID of the account (if account-level job).
  * `zone_id` — ID of the zone (if zone-level job).
  * `name` — Name of the Logpush job.
  * `enabled` — Boolean flag indicating whether the job is enabled.
  * `destination_conf` — Destination configuration string (destination URL/path).
  * `dataset` — Dataset type being pushed (e.g., `http_requests`, `firewall_events`, `workers_trace_events`)[4].
  * `logpull_options` — Options or field selections applied to the logs.
  * `frequency` — Push frequency (e.g., `high`).
  * `error_message` — Last error message encountered by the job, if any.
  * `last_complete` — Timestamp of the last successful log push.
  * Standard Steampipe meta columns (`title`, `conn`, `_ctx`).

SELECT

For the **Steampipe Cloudflare plugin**, configuration is managed using HCL within `.spc` connection files (typically located at `~/.steampipe/config/cloudflare.spc`)[1]. 

### 1. Connection Configuration (`.spc`)
An API token is the recommended authentication method[1]. Write permissions are **not** required to query infrastructure data—only **Read** permissions are needed[1].

```hcl
connection "cloudflare" {
  plugin = "cloudflare"
  token  = "your-cloudflare-api-token-here"
}
```

Alternatively, you can provide it via environment variables (e.g., `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`)[2].

---

### 2. Required API Token Permissions
To successfully query various Cloudflare resources (such as zones, DNS records, accounts, and analytics)[1], your Cloudflare API token must be generated with appropriate **Read-level** permissions depending on the tables/features you plan to query. 

General guidelines for token setup:
* **Principle of Least Privilege:** Only grant permissions for the specific features/resources you intend to query[3].
* **Read Access Only:** Ensure permissions are restricted to **Read** operations (write access is unnecessary for Steampipe's inspection and querying capabilities)[1].
* **Resource Scoping:** Scope the token to specific Accounts or Zones where applicable, rather than opening it globally across all resources[3].

In **Powerpipe**, controls defined within `.pp` mod files rely on an SQL query to evaluate resources against security or configuration standards[1][2]. Every control's SQL query **must return specific required columns**, including a `status` column[1].

### Required Control Columns in SQL
Your SQL query must return at least the following standard columns[1]:
1. **`resource`** (String): A unique identifier for the targeted resource (e.g., an ARN, ID, or file path)[1].
2. **`status`** (String): The evaluation result for that specific resource row[1]. 
3. **`reason`** (String): A descriptive sentence ending with a period detailing *why* the resource has that status[1].

---

### Valid Control Statuses
When writing your SQL `CASE` statement to assign a `status`, you must use one of the officially defined Powerpipe control statuses[1]:

* **`ok`**: The resource is compliant with the control[1].
* **`alarm`**: The resource is *not* compliant and requires remediation[1].
* **`skip`**: The control or resource was not evaluated because Powerpipe (or conditional logic) was instructed to skip it[1].
* **`info`**: The control is non-automated, requiring manual verification or providing supplemental context[1].
* **`error`**: Automatically used or triggered if an exception/error occurs while calculating the state[1].

---

### Example Usage in a `.pp` Mod File

Here is an example of a custom control block in a `.pp` file demonstrating how an SQL query outputs `ok`, `alarm`, or `skip` statuses[2][3]:

```hcl
control "s3_bucket_encryption_enabled" {
  title       = "S3 buckets should have default encryption enabled"
  description = "Ensure that all S3 buckets are configured with server-side encryption."
  
  sql = <<-EOT
    select
      arn as resource,
      case
        -- Example condition to conditionally skip checking a bucket
        when lifecycle_status = 'SUSPENDED' then 'skip'
        when server_side_encryption_configuration is null then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      case
        when lifecycle_status = 'SUSPENDED' then 'Bucket is suspended; evaluation skipped.'
        when server_side_encryption_configuration is null then title || ' does not have server-side encryption enabled.'
        else title || ' has server-side encryption enabled.'
      end as reason,
      region,
      account_id
    from
      aws_s3_bucket;
  EOT
}
```

In Steampipe's Cloudflare plugin, credentials can be configured directly inside your connection configuration files (typically located at `~/.steampipe/config/cloudflare.spc` with a `.spc` extension) or passed via environment variables[1].

### Credential Resolution Order
Steampipe resolves Cloudflare credentials in the following order[1]:

1. `token` defined in the Steampipe config (`.spc`)[1]
2. `email` and `api_key` defined in the Steampipe config (`.spc`)[1]
3. **`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`** environment variable[1]
4. `CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY` environment variables[1]
5. `CF_API_TOKEN` environment variable[1]
6. `CF_API_EMAIL` and `CF_API_KEY` environment variables[1]

### Example Configuration (`.spc`)

Using an explicit token inside a `.spc` file[1]:

```hcl
connection "cloudflare" {
  plugin = "cloudflare"
  token  = "REDACTED"
}
```

Alternatively, if you leave the token out of the `.spc` file, Steampipe will automatically pick up the **`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`** environment variable from your shell[1]:

```bash
export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN="REDACTED"
steampipe query
```

In Powerpipe, the `mod.pp` configuration file uses a `mod` block with a `require` block to declare prerequisites such as the minimum Powerpipe version, dependent mods, and required plugins (like the Cloudflare plugin)[1].

### `mod.pp` Syntax for a Cloudflare Plugin and Benchmark Mod

```hcl
mod "cloudflare_custom_mod" {
  title       = "Cloudflare Custom Mod"
  description = "Custom dashboards, controls, and benchmarks for Cloudflare using Powerpipe."
  color       = "#F38020" // Cloudflare orange accent

  require {
    powerpipe {
      min_version = "1.0.0"
    }

    # Declare the required Steampipe Cloudflare plugin
    plugin "cloudflare" {
      min_version = "1.6.0"
    }

    # Optional: You can also require other upstream compliance or insight mods if needed
    # mod "github.com/turbot/steampipe-mod-cloudflare-compliance" {
    #   version = "*"
    # }
  }
}
```[1][2]

### Key Syntax Elements:
1. **`mod "mod_name"`**: Defines the root identifier for your custom Powerpipe mod using lower snake case[1].
2. **`require { ... }`**: Encapsulates all constraints and dependencies necessary for the mod to compile and run[1].
3. **`plugin "cloudflare"`**: Specifies that the Steampipe `cloudflare` plugin is required[1][3], alongside an optional `min_version` constraint[1]. 

### Related Setup Commands:
* **Initialize a mod** (creates the template `mod.pp` file):
  ```bash
  powerpipe mod init
  ```[4]
* **Install dependencies** (reads `mod.pp` to fetch requirements):
  ```bash
  powerpipe mod install
  ```[4]
* **Run a benchmark** defined within your mod or its dependencies:
  ```bash
  powerpipe benchmark run <benchmark_name>
  ```[5]

control "submission_worker_no_logpush" {
  title       = "Submission Worker scripts must have Logpush disabled"
  description = "SPEC §5.3 / §7 and GDPR Art. 25 require SurveyBeat's Submission Worker to keep Logpush off so submission requests are never exported to log pipelines."
  severity    = "critical"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with submission_workers as (
      select
        id,
        account_id,
        logpush
      from
        cloudflare_worker_script
      where
        id ilike '%submission%'
    )
    select
      w.id as resource,
      case
        when w.logpush is true then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      case
        when w.logpush is true then 'Submission Worker ' || w.id || ' has logpush enabled.'
        else 'Submission Worker ' || w.id || ' has logpush disabled.'
      end as reason
    from
      submission_workers as w
    union all
    select
      a.id as resource,
      'info' as status,
      'No Submission Worker scripts (*submission*) found in account ' || a.name || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account as a
    where
      not exists (select 1 from submission_workers);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "WorkerPrivacy"
  })
}

control "submission_worker_no_tail_consumers" {
  title       = "Submission Worker scripts must have no tail consumers attached"
  description = "SPEC §5.3 / §7 and GDPR Art. 25 require SurveyBeat's Submission Worker to attach zero tail consumers, as tail events carry unredacted client IP headers and request metadata."
  severity    = "critical"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with submission_workers as (
      select
        id,
        account_id,
        tail_consumers
      from
        cloudflare_worker_script
      where
        id ilike '%submission%'
    )
    select
      w.id as resource,
      case
        when jsonb_array_length(coalesce(w.tail_consumers, '[]'::jsonb)) > 0 then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      case
        when jsonb_array_length(coalesce(w.tail_consumers, '[]'::jsonb)) > 0
          then 'Submission Worker ' || w.id || ' has ' || jsonb_array_length(w.tail_consumers) || ' tail consumer(s) attached.'
        else 'Submission Worker ' || w.id || ' has no tail consumers attached.'
      end as reason
    from
      submission_workers as w
    union all
    select
      a.id as resource,
      'info' as status,
      'No Submission Worker scripts (*submission*) found in account ' || a.name || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account as a
    where
      not exists (select 1 from submission_workers);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "WorkerPrivacy"
  })
}

control "logpush_no_unfiltered_submission_pii" {
  title       = "Logpush jobs must not export ClientIP/ClientRequestURI for Submission hosts or workers_trace_events"
  description = "Per docs/research/workers-logging-privacy.md §5 and GDPR Art. 25, enabled HTTP request Logpush jobs must filter out submit.* hosts or omit ClientIP/ClientRequestURI, and workers_trace_events should not capture Submission requests."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with jobs as (
      select
        id::text as job_id,
        coalesce(name, id::text) as job_name,
        dataset,
        enabled,
        coalesce(logpull_options, '') as logpull_options,
        coalesce(output_options::text, '') as output_options_text
      from
        cloudflare_logpush_job
    )
    select
      j.job_id as resource,
      case
        when not j.enabled then 'ok'
        when j.dataset = 'workers_trace_events' then 'alarm'
        when j.dataset = 'http_requests'
          and (j.logpull_options ilike '%ClientIP%' or j.logpull_options ilike '%ClientRequestURI%' or j.output_options_text ilike '%ClientIP%' or j.output_options_text ilike '%ClientRequestURI%')
          then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      case
        when not j.enabled then 'Logpush job ' || j.job_name || ' (' || j.dataset || ') is disabled.'
        when j.dataset = 'workers_trace_events'
          then 'Enabled Logpush job ' || j.job_name || ' exports workers_trace_events; verify Submission Workers have logpush=false.'
        when j.dataset = 'http_requests'
          and (j.logpull_options ilike '%ClientIP%' or j.logpull_options ilike '%ClientRequestURI%' or j.output_options_text ilike '%ClientIP%' or j.output_options_text ilike '%ClientRequestURI%')
          then 'Enabled http_requests Logpush job ' || j.job_name || ' includes ClientIP or ClientRequestURI; ensure submit.* host is filtered out or fields are omitted.'
        else 'Enabled Logpush job ' || j.job_name || ' (' || j.dataset || ') does not export ClientIP/ClientRequestURI.'
      end as reason
    from
      jobs as j
    union all
    select
      a.id as resource,
      'ok' as status,
      'No Logpush jobs configured in account ' || a.name || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account as a
    where
      not exists (select 1 from jobs);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "LogPrivacy"
  })
}

control "zone_ssl_strict" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should enforce Full (strict) SSL/TLS mode"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.7 require end-to-end encrypted transport with origin certificate validation (ssl = 'strict')."
  severity    = "critical"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value = 'strict' then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      z.name || ' SSL/TLS mode is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'ssl';
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "EncryptionInTransit"
  })
}

control "zone_min_tls_version" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should enforce minimum TLS version 1.2 or 1.3"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.7 disallow deprecated TLS 1.0 and 1.1 protocols."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value in ('1.2', '1.3') then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      z.name || ' minimum TLS version is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'min_tls_version';
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "EncryptionInTransit"
  })
}

control "zone_tls_1_3_enabled" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should have TLS 1.3 enabled"
  description = "Enforces modern cipher suites and forward secrecy for GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.7."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value in ('on', 'zrt') then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      z.name || ' TLS 1.3 setting is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'tls_1_3';
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "EncryptionInTransit"
  })
}

control "zone_always_use_https" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should enable Always Use HTTPS"
  description = "Redirects all plaintext HTTP requests to HTTPS at the edge (GDPR Art. 32, SOC 2 CC6.7)."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value = 'on' then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      z.name || ' Always Use HTTPS is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'always_use_https';
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "EncryptionInTransit"
  })
}

control "zone_automatic_https_rewrites" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should enable Automatic HTTPS Rewrites"
  description = "Prevents mixed-content leaks by rewriting insecure HTTP links to HTTPS (GDPR Art. 32, SOC 2 CC6.7)."
  severity    = "low"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value = 'on' then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      z.name || ' Automatic HTTPS Rewrites is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'automatic_https_rewrites';
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "EncryptionInTransit"
  })
}

control "zone_hsts_enabled" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should enable HSTS with max-age >= 6 months and nosniff"
  description = "Enforces HTTP Strict Transport Security so browsers refuse downgrade attacks on surveybeat.app (GDPR Art. 32, SOC 2 CC6.7)."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with parsed as (
      select
        z.id,
        z.name,
        case
          when s.value is not null and s.value ~ '^\\s*\\{' then s.value::jsonb -> 'strict_transport_security'
          else null
        end as hsts
      from
        cloudflare_zone as z
        left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
          on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'security_header'
    )
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when hsts is null then 'alarm'
        when coalesce((hsts ->> 'enabled')::boolean, false) is false then 'alarm'
        when coalesce((hsts ->> 'max_age')::bigint, 0) < 15552000 then 'alarm'
        when coalesce((hsts ->> 'nosniff')::boolean, false) is false then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      case
        when hsts is null then name || ' has no security_header HSTS configuration.'
        when coalesce((hsts ->> 'enabled')::boolean, false) is false then name || ' has HSTS disabled.'
        when coalesce((hsts ->> 'max_age')::bigint, 0) < 15552000
          then name || ' HSTS max_age is ' || coalesce(hsts ->> 'max_age', '0') || 's (expected >= 15552000s).'
        when coalesce((hsts ->> 'nosniff')::boolean, false) is false
          then name || ' HSTS has X-Content-Type-Options nosniff disabled.'
        else name || ' has HSTS enabled (max_age=' || (hsts ->> 'max_age') || 's, include_subdomains=' || coalesce(hsts ->> 'include_subdomains', 'false') || ', nosniff=true).'
      end as reason
    from
      parsed;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "EncryptionInTransit"
  })
}

control "zone_waf_enabled" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should have WAF rulesets or WAF protection enabled"
  description = "SOC 2 CC6.6 and GDPR Art. 32 require Web Application Firewall filtering to block common edge exploits."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with waf_rulesets as (
      select
        zone_id,
        count(*) as ruleset_count
      from
        cloudflare_ruleset
      where
        zone_id is not null
        and phase in (
          'http_request_firewall_managed',
          'http_request_firewall_custom',
          'http_ratelimit'
        )
      group by
        zone_id
    )
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value = 'on' or coalesce(r.ruleset_count, 0) > 0 then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      case
        when coalesce(r.ruleset_count, 0) > 0
          then z.name || ' has ' || r.ruleset_count || ' active WAF/rate-limit ruleset(s) (legacy waf=' || coalesce(s.value, 'unset') || ').'
        when s.value = 'on'
          then z.name || ' has legacy WAF setting enabled.'
        else z.name || ' has no WAF rulesets and WAF setting is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'waf'
      left join waf_rulesets as r
        on r.zone_id = z.id;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "BoundaryProtection"
  })
}

control "zone_browser_check_enabled" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should enable Browser Integrity Check"
  description = "SOC 2 CC6.6 defense-in-depth check that inspects HTTP headers for abusive clients and automated scanners."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value = 'on' then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      z.name || ' Browser Integrity Check is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'browser_check';
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "BoundaryProtection"
  })
}

control "zone_security_level_appropriate" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should not set Security Level to essentially_off"
  description = "Ensures baseline IP reputation challenge protection remains enabled for SOC 2 CC6.6."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when s.value is null or s.value = 'essentially_off' then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      z.name || ' Security Level is ' || coalesce(s.value, 'not set') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join cloudflare_zone_setting as s
        on s.zone_id = z.id and s.id = 'security_level';
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "BoundaryProtection"
  })
}

control "zone_leaked_credential_check" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should enable Leaked Credential Checks where plan supports it"
  description = "Detects compromised credentials at the edge (SOC 2 CC6.6)."
  severity    = "low"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when leaked_credential_check_enabled is true then 'ok'
        else 'info'
      end as status,
      case
        when leaked_credential_check_enabled is true
          then name || ' has Leaked Credential Check enabled.'
        else name || ' has Leaked Credential Check disabled (verify plan eligibility).'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "BoundaryProtection"
  })
}

control "zone_security_txt_configured" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should publish RFC 9116 security.txt"
  description = "SOC 2 CC7.2 vulnerability disclosure readiness: publishes security contact metadata at /.well-known/security.txt."
  severity    = "low"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when coalesce((security_txt ->> 'enabled')::boolean, false) is true then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      case
        when coalesce((security_txt ->> 'enabled')::boolean, false) is true
          then name || ' publishes security.txt.'
        else name || ' does not have security.txt enabled.'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "VulnerabilityManagement"
  })
}

control "zone_active_not_paused" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones must be active and not paused"
  description = "SOC 2 A1.2 / CC6.6: pausing a zone bypasses Cloudflare proxy, WAF, and TLS protections."
  severity    = "critical"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when status = 'active' and coalesce(paused, false) is false then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      name || ' status is ' || coalesce(status, 'unknown') || ', paused=' || coalesce(paused::text, 'false') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "Availability"
  })
}

control "zone_not_development_mode" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones must not remain in Development Mode"
  description = "SOC 2 A1.2 / CC8.1: Development Mode temporarily bypasses Cloudflare edge caching and increases origin exposure."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when coalesce(development_mode, 0) = 0 then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      case
        when coalesce(development_mode, 0) = 0 then name || ' is not in Development Mode.'
        else name || ' has Development Mode active (' || development_mode || 's remaining).'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "Availability"
  })
}

control "zone_dnssec_enabled" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should have DNSSEC active"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.6: DNSSEC protects surveybeat.app against DNS spoofing and cache poisoning."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when dnssec ->> 'status' = 'active' then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      name || ' DNSSEC status is ' || coalesce(dnssec ->> 'status', 'disabled') || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "DNSIntegrity"
  })
}

control "dns_caa_record_configured" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should define CAA DNS records"
  description = "SOC 2 CC6.6: Certification Authority Authorization (CAA) records restrict which CAs may issue TLS certificates for surveybeat.app."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with caa as (
      select
        zone_id,
        count(*) as caa_count
      from
        cloudflare_dns_record
      where
        type = 'CAA'
      group by
        zone_id
    )
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when coalesce(c.caa_count, 0) > 0 then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      case
        when coalesce(c.caa_count, 0) > 0 then z.name || ' has ' || c.caa_count || ' CAA record(s).'
        else z.name || ' has no CAA records configured.'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join caa as c
        on c.zone_id = z.id;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "DNSIntegrity"
  })
}

control "dns_email_auth_records" {
  title       = "Cloudflare zones should publish SPF and DMARC DNS records"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.6: protects SurveyBeat invitation and email-code sign-in flows from domain spoofing."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with txt as (
      select
        zone_id,
        bool_or(name = zone_name and content ilike 'v=spf1%') as has_root_spf,
        bool_or(name like '_dmarc.%' and content ilike 'v=DMARC1%') as has_root_dmarc,
        bool_or(name like 'notify.%' and content ilike 'v=spf1%') as has_notify_spf,
        bool_or(name like '_dmarc.notify.%' and content ilike 'v=DMARC1%') as has_notify_dmarc
      from
        cloudflare_dns_record
      where
        type = 'TXT'
      group by
        zone_id
    )
    select
      z.id as resource,
      case
        when coalesce(t.has_root_spf, false) and coalesce(t.has_root_dmarc, false) then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      z.name
        || ' root SPF=' || coalesce(t.has_root_spf::text, 'false')
        || ', root DMARC=' || coalesce(t.has_root_dmarc::text, 'false')
        || ', notify SPF=' || coalesce(t.has_notify_spf::text, 'false')
        || ', notify DMARC=' || coalesce(t.has_notify_dmarc::text, 'false')
        || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
      left join txt as t
        on t.zone_id = z.id;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "EmailSecurity"
  })
}

control "dns_sensitive_records_proxied" {
  title       = "SurveyBeat web and submission DNS records must be proxied through Cloudflare"
  description = "Ensures A/AAAA/CNAME records for surveybeat.app, dashboard, and submit hosts route through Cloudflare WAF and TLS termination (GDPR Art. 32, SOC 2 CC6.6)."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with app_records as (
      select
        id,
        zone_name,
        name,
        type,
        proxied,
        proxiable
      from
        cloudflare_dns_record
      where
        type in ('A', 'AAAA', 'CNAME')
        and proxiable is true
        and (
          name = zone_name
          or name like 'www.%'
          or name like 'app.%'
          or name like 'dashboard.%'
          or name like 'submit.%'
          or name like 'staging.%'
        )
    )
    select
      r.id as resource,
      case
        when r.proxied is true then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      r.type || ' record ' || r.name || ' is ' || case when r.proxied is true then 'proxied.' else 'DNS-only (unproxied).' end as reason
    from
      app_records as r
    union all
    select
      z.id as resource,
      'info' as status,
      'No proxiable app/submit A, AAAA, or CNAME DNS records found in zone ' || z.name || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_zone as z
    where
      not exists (select 1 from app_records);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "BoundaryProtection"
  })
}

control "account_enforce_twofactor" {
  title       = "Cloudflare accounts must enforce two-factor authentication for all members"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.1 require multi-factor authentication on administrative control-plane access."
  severity    = "critical"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when coalesce((settings ->> 'enforce_twofactor')::boolean, false) is true then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      case
        when coalesce((settings ->> 'enforce_twofactor')::boolean, false) is true
          then 'Account ' || name || ' enforces two-factor authentication.'
        else 'Account ' || name || ' does not enforce two-factor authentication (settings.enforce_twofactor=' || coalesce(settings ->> 'enforce_twofactor', 'unset') || ').'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "AccessControl"
  })
}

control "user_mfa_enabled" {
  title       = "Authenticated Cloudflare user must have two-factor authentication enabled"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.1 require MFA on the Cloudflare user context."
  severity    = "critical"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when two_factor_authentication_enabled is true then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      case
        when two_factor_authentication_enabled is true
          then 'User ' || coalesce(email, id) || ' has 2FA enabled.'
        else 'User ' || coalesce(email, id) || ' does not have 2FA enabled.'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_user;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "AccessControl"
  })
}

control "account_member_accepted_and_mfa" {
  title       = "Cloudflare account members should be accepted and have 2FA enabled"
  description = "SOC 2 CC6.1 / CC6.2: identifies stale pending invitations and account members lacking 2FA."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    select
      id as resource,
      case
        when status <> 'accepted' then 'alarm'
        when coalesce((user ->> 'two_factor_authentication_enabled')::boolean, false) is false then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      coalesce(user_email, id)
        || ' membership status=' || coalesce(status, 'unknown')
        || ', 2FA=' || coalesce(user ->> 'two_factor_authentication_enabled', 'unknown')
        || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account_member;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "AccessControl"
  })
}

control "api_token_expiration_set" {
  title       = "Active Cloudflare API tokens should have an expiration date"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.1 / CC6.2: non-expiring API tokens increase blast radius of credential exposure."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with tokens as (
      select
        id,
        name,
        status,
        expires_on
      from
        cloudflare_api_token
    )
    select
      t.id as resource,
      case
        when t.status <> 'active' then 'skip'
        when t.expires_on is null then 'alarm'
        when t.expires_on <= now() then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      case
        when t.status <> 'active' then 'API token ' || t.name || ' is ' || t.status || '.'
        when t.expires_on is null then 'Active API token ' || t.name || ' has no expiration date.'
        when t.expires_on <= now() then 'API token ' || t.name || ' expired at ' || t.expires_on::text || '.'
        else 'Active API token ' || t.name || ' expires on ' || t.expires_on::text || '.'
      end as reason
    from
      tokens as t
    union all
    select
      u.id as resource,
      'info' as status,
      'No user-scoped API tokens visible to current credential (token may lack User:API Tokens:Read or be account-owned).' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_user as u
    where
      not exists (select 1 from tokens);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "CredentialHygiene"
  })
}

control "api_token_ip_condition" {
  title       = "Active Cloudflare API tokens should document IP allowlist conditions where feasible"
  description = "SOC 2 CC6.1 defense-in-depth: checks whether active API tokens restrict client IP ranges (informational when used by dynamic GitHub-hosted runners)."
  severity    = "low"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with tokens as (
      select
        id,
        name,
        status,
        condition
      from
        cloudflare_api_token
    )
    select
      t.id as resource,
      case
        when t.status <> 'active' then 'skip'
        when t.condition -> 'request_ip' is not null then 'ok'
        else 'info'
      end as status,
      case
        when t.status <> 'active' then 'API token ' || t.name || ' is ' || t.status || '.'
        when t.condition -> 'request_ip' is not null then 'API token ' || t.name || ' restricts client IPs.'
        else 'API token ' || t.name || ' has no IP address condition configured (expected for dynamic CI runners; restrict if static).'
      end as reason
    from
      tokens as t
    union all
    select
      u.id as resource,
      'info' as status,
      'No user-scoped API tokens visible to current credential.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_user as u
    where
      not exists (select 1 from tokens);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "CredentialHygiene"
  })
}

control "access_policy_no_unrestricted_bypass" {
  title       = "Cloudflare Access policies must not grant unrestricted everyone bypass/allow"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 CC6.1: ensures Zero Trust Access applications do not bypass authentication for everyone."
  severity    = "high"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with policies as (
      select
        id,
        name,
        application_name,
        decision,
        include
      from
        cloudflare_access_policy
    )
    select
      p.id as resource,
      case
        when p.decision in ('allow', 'bypass') and p.include::text ilike '%"everyone"%' then 'alarm'
        else 'ok'
      end as status,
      case
        when p.decision in ('allow', 'bypass') and p.include::text ilike '%"everyone"%'
          then 'Access policy ' || p.name || ' on ' || coalesce(p.application_name, 'application') || ' has decision=' || p.decision || ' for everyone.'
        else 'Access policy ' || p.name || ' (' || p.decision || ') does not allow/bypass everyone.'
      end as reason
    from
      policies as p
    union all
    select
      a.id as resource,
      'ok' as status,
      'No Cloudflare Access policies configured in account ' || a.name || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account as a
    where
      not exists (select 1 from policies);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "AccessControl"
  })
}

control "account_notification_policy_configured" {
  title       = "Cloudflare account should have at least one enabled notification policy"
  description = "GDPR Art. 33 and SOC 2 CC7.2 require automated alerting for security events, DDoS, SSL/TLS expiration, or service health."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with enabled_policies as (
      select
        account_id,
        count(*) as policy_count
      from
        cloudflare_notification_policy
      where
        enabled is true
      group by
        account_id
    )
    select
      a.id as resource,
      case
        when coalesce(p.policy_count, 0) > 0 then 'ok'
        else 'alarm'
      end as status,
      case
        when coalesce(p.policy_count, 0) > 0
          then 'Account ' || a.name || ' has ' || p.policy_count || ' enabled notification policy(ies).'
        else 'Account ' || a.name || ' has no enabled Cloudflare notification policies.'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account as a
      left join enabled_policies as p
        on p.account_id = a.id;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "Monitoring"
  })
}

control "audit_log_active" {
  title       = "Cloudflare user audit logs should be readable and active"
  description = "GDPR Art. 33 and SOC 2 CC7.2 / CC8.1 require verifiable audit trails of configuration changes."
  severity    = "medium"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with recent as (
      select
        count(*) as event_count,
        max("when") as latest_event
      from
        cloudflare_user_audit_log
    )
    select
      a.id as resource,
      case
        when r.event_count > 0 then 'ok'
        else 'info'
      end as status,
      case
        when r.event_count > 0
          then 'Audit log readable for account ' || a.name || ' (' || r.event_count || ' events fetched; latest at ' || r.latest_event::text || ').'
        else 'No audit log events returned for account ' || a.name || '.'
      end as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account as a
      cross join recent as r;
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "AuditLogging"
  })
}

control "r2_bucket_inventory_encryption" {
  title       = "Cloudflare R2 buckets should be inventoried and free of unencrypted custom overrides"
  description = "GDPR Art. 32 and SOC 2 A1.2: Cloudflare R2 encrypts objects at rest by default; verifies bucket inventory and server-side encryption configuration."
  severity    = "low"

  sql = <<-EOQ
    with buckets as (
      select
        account_id,
        name,
        region,
        server_side_encryption_configuration
      from
        cloudflare_r2_bucket
    )
    select
      b.name as resource,
      'ok' as status,
      'R2 bucket ' || b.name || ' (region=' || coalesce(b.region, 'auto') || ') uses Cloudflare R2 encryption at rest.' as reason
    from
      buckets as b
    union all
    select
      a.id as resource,
      'ok' as status,
      'No R2 buckets provisioned in account ' || a.name || '.' as reason
    from
      cloudflare_account as a
    where
      not exists (select 1 from buckets);
  EOQ

  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    gdpr     = "true"
    soc2     = "true"
    category = "Storage"
  })
}

# SurveyBeat Cloudflare Compliance (Steampipe + Powerpipe)

This Powerpipe mod audits SurveyBeat's Cloudflare infrastructure using the Steampipe [`turbot/cloudflare`](https://hub.steampipe.io/plugins/turbot/cloudflare) plugin against **GDPR** (Articles 5, 25, 32, 33) and **SOC 2** Trust Services Criteria (CC6, CC7, CC8, A1).

## Prerequisites

1. Install Steampipe, Powerpipe, and the `cloudflare` plugin:
   ```sh
   sudo /bin/sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://steampipe.io/install/steampipe.sh)"
   sudo /bin/sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://powerpipe.io/install/powerpipe.sh)"
   steampipe plugin install cloudflare
   ```
2. Configure a **read-only** Cloudflare API token (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) with:
   - Account: `Account Settings:Read`, `Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups:Read`, `Notifications:Read`, `Workers Scripts:Read`, `R2 Storage:Read`, `Logs:Read`
   - Zone (`surveybeat.app`): `Zone:Read`, `Zone Settings:Read`, `DNS:Read`, `Firewall Services:Read`, `Logs:Read`
   - User: `User Details:Read`, `API Tokens:Read`, `Audit Logs:Read`
3. Start Steampipe with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` in the environment (or set `token` in `~/.steampipe/config/cloudflare.spc`):
   ```sh
   steampipe service restart
   ```

## Running benchmarks

```sh
# All GDPR + SOC 2 controls
powerpipe benchmark run --mod-location infra/compliance all_compliance

# GDPR only
powerpipe benchmark run --mod-location infra/compliance gdpr

# SOC 2 only
powerpipe benchmark run --mod-location infra/compliance soc2

# Or via the repo wrapper (also runs Workers observability check when --stage is passed)
pnpm check:compliance
pnpm check:compliance -- --stage production
```

## Coverage boundary (`turbot/cloudflare` vs SurveyBeat scripts)

`turbot/steampipe-plugin-cloudflare` covers account/user IAM, API tokens, zones, zone settings, DNS, WAF rulesets, Worker scripts/routes, Logpush jobs, R2 buckets, notification policies, and Access policies.

It does **not** currently expose tables for Workers Observability (`observability.logs` / `traces` / `invocation_logs`), D1, Durable Objects, Queues, AI Gateway, or Email Sending. Those privacy invariants remain enforced by:
- `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` (`infra/scripts/check-observability.ts`)
- `pnpm test:preview-privacy --stage <stage>` (`infra/tests/privacy/canary-sweep.ts`)
- `pnpm test:privacy` (`*.privacy.test.ts` across packages)

args.CommandLine: powerpipe benchmark list --mod-location infra/compliance && powerpipe benchmark run --mod-location infra/compliance all_compliance --dry-run
